# Per: Performance

Every entry in this section of the official C++ Core Guidelines, in their order. Each link opens the official text. "ours" links the pages of this repo that cite the rule; "example" and "test" link our own example and unit test for it.

[Official section](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#s-performance) · [All sections](README.md)

- [Per.1: Don't optimize without reason](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-reason) · ours: [core-guidelines](../core-guidelines.md), [performance-tooling](../performance-tooling.md) · no example: the rule is about deciding whether a speed-up is needed at all (a requirement, a measured problem), which no code pattern shows.
- [Per.2: Don't optimize prematurely](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-knuth) · ours: [core-guidelines](../core-guidelines.md), [performance-tooling](../performance-tooling.md) · no example: the rule is about when to optimize (after the design works and a profile points somewhere), not about how code is written.
- [Per.3: Don't optimize something that's not performance critical](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-critical) · no example: which code is critical is found by profiling the whole program, not by reading a snippet.
- [Per.4: Don't assume that complicated code is necessarily faster than simple code](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-simple) · ours: [core-guidelines](../core-guidelines.md) · [example](examples/performance.md#per4-dont-assume-that-complicated-code-is-necessarily-faster-than-simple-code)
- [Per.5: Don't assume that low-level code is necessarily faster than high-level code](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-low) · ours: [core-guidelines](../core-guidelines.md) · [example](examples/performance.md#per5-dont-assume-that-low-level-code-is-necessarily-faster-than-high-level-code)
- [Per.6: Don't make claims about performance without measurements](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rper-measure) · ours: [core-guidelines](../core-guidelines.md), [performance-tooling](../performance-tooling.md) · no example: the rule is about backing claims with benchmarks and profiles (Google Benchmark, `perf`, a `<chrono>` timer), not about the code being measured.
